answer: In this PoA design, each identity must complete a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, with each result depending on the previous one; a verifier checks the output using a Wesolowski proof. An attacker may run clone chains on separate GPUs, but cannot parallelize the squarings within any chain, so every additional identity incurs its own elapsed-time and compute cost. Like a canyon crossed step by step, neither marble nor yarrow can shortcut the dependency.
